clue.text: Well protected, gum-shield and all?

parts.note: a fully equipped fighter is heavily armed; the gum-shield jokily takes the idiom literally, as if even the mouth were kitted out

explanation.surface: A boxer kitted out with mouthguard and every other bit of protective gear.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone carrying every possible weapon, and the gum-shield nods at the dental half of the phrase.

clue.text: Substitutes for missing members

parts.note: reads like replacement players for absent club members, but the members are arms and legs

explanation.surface: A sports club calling up reserves for players who failed to turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' wants to mean people in a club or team; here it is the old sense of limbs of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosthetic arms and legs replace lost body parts, which is what a prosthesis does.

clue.text: Game of wits

explanation.surface: A board or puzzle game that tests your brains.
explanation.definitionFit: Marbles is a children's game played with glass balls, and losing your marbles is losing your sanity or mental faculties.

clue.text: An opening celebration or its finale

indicators.note: says the word or comes at the end of the celebration word, finishing it off

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party or celebration

explanation.surface: The start of a party, or how it ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its finale' tells you OR is attached to the end of DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorway is a gap in a wall you pass through, an entrance.

clue.text: Crime of a receiver of stolen goods

parts.note: taken as written
a fence is slang for someone who buys and sells stolen property

explanation.surface: Defining the criminal act committed by someone handling stolen loot.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is a breach of the law, a synonym for a criminal act.

clue.text: He has a fish for curing

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A man keeps a fish in brine to preserve it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curing' suggests salting fish, but it means making well.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean making a sick person well again, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Long stitch may fasten a carpet

explanation.surface: Sewing and carpet-fitting share a single fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacking is loose temporary sewing with long stitches, and a tack is a short nail used to hold carpet down.

clue.text: The scholar takes ages to sum up

parts.note: eras are long periods of time, ages

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word sum is read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: An academic spends a long time producing a summary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SUM to MUS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus was the Dutch Renaissance humanist, the most famous learned man of his day.

clue.text: Part of London Transport for hire?

definitions.text: Part of London Transport for hire?

parts.note: Hackney is a borough in north-east London
a carriage is a vehicle, a means of transport

explanation.surface: Asking which piece of the capital's public transport network can be hired.
explanation.walkthrough: London Transport looks like the name of the old transport authority; split it, as HACKNEY is a London borough. A hackney carriage is the official name for a London black cab.
explanation.definitionFit: The licensed taxi you hail in London's streets is legally a vehicle plying for hire.

clue.text: Change course when the vessel's caught in the swell

indicators.note: says the vessel is trapped within the swell, placed inside it

parts.note: a swell is an old word for a smartly dressed upper-class person, a toff
an urn is a vase or vessel

explanation.surface: A ship turns away when caught in heavy seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' and 'swell' paint a ship in rough water; the vessel is a vase and the swell a posh person.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave one road for another is to alter direction, which is a change of route.

clue.text: Bill includes a broken chair that's antique

indicators.note: the bill holds the broken chair within it

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: the chair has been smashed up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An invoice listing a damaged old chair from a dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' is a common crossword signal for AC (account); 'broken' scrambles the chair, and 'includes' wraps the bill round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean very old or belonging to an earlier time, as synonyms.

clue.text: Seasonal slump in America?

parts.note: reads as a downturn in the US economy at some time of year; it is a drop, and also the American name for autumn

explanation.surface: An economic dip that hits the United States every year.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop or decline is a slump, and in the US the season after summer bears the same name.

clue.text: Dismantle a United Nations oil installation?

parts.note: a rig is a platform for drilling oil

explanation.surface: Asking whether to take apart a drilling platform owned by the UN.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip a ship of its rigging is to take its gear apart.

clue.text: Circle an island sultanate

parts.note: a circle looks like the letter O
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Sail round a small island ruled by a sultan.
explanation.definitionFit: Oman is a Middle Eastern country ruled by a sultan.

clue.text: Major eastern state of USA

parts.note: main means chief or principal, major
E is the abbreviation for east or eastern

explanation.surface: Naming a big state on the American east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is the north-easternmost US state, in New England.

clue.text: Letter from Greece is sent up with a note to mother

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the word is is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: G is a note of the musical scale
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A letter posted from Greece, with a note added for Mum.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Fall of rotter in law-suit

indicators.note: places the rotter within the lawsuit

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit brought in court
a cad is an old word for a dishonourable man, a rotter

explanation.surface: The downfall of a scoundrel caught up in court action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' suggests disgrace; it means a waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterfall tumbling in stages is a cascade, so the noun is a synonym.

clue.text: Deny a saying is wrong

indicators.note: the phrase a saying is made wrong, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Contradict a proverb by declaring it false.
explanation.definitionFit: To contradict or dispute a claim is to refuse it as untrue, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Girl able to recall a whole lot of dates

parts.note: Alma is a girl's name

indicators.note: recalling is calling back, so the word for able runs backwards

parts.note: can means is able to

explanation.surface: A woman with a remarkable memory for every date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to recall' turns CAN into NAC. 'dates' suggests a sweetheart's diary or fruit; it is calendar days.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a yearly calendar listing days, events and astronomical data.

clue.text: After false alarm, one receives a complaint

indicators.note: puts what follows after the jumbled alarm
a false alarm is a fake one, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
taken as written

explanation.surface: After a scare that turns out groundless, someone lodges a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false' turns ALARM into MALAR. 'complaint' means an illness, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaria is a disease, and a complaint can mean an ailment or illness.

clue.text: Can veto conversion into foreign currency

indicators.note: converting changes the form of the letters of can veto, rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone may block the exchange of money into another currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A centavo is a small coin, a hundredth of the peso or real in Latin American countries.

clue.text: A good man helped to put it on the map

definitions.text: A good man helped to put it on the map

parts.words: A good man helped to put it on the map
parts.note: refers to the parable of the Good Samaritan, whose fame spread the name of his homeland

explanation.surface: A kindly man made some place famous.
explanation.walkthrough: The Good Samaritan of Jesus's parable came from this region of ancient Palestine.
explanation.definitionFit: The region gave its name to the Samaritans, so the parable made the place widely known.

clue.text: This leg break shows quickness of the hand

indicators.note: a leg break in cricket is a spinning ball; here break means the letters of this leg are broken up

explanation.surface: A bowler's leg-break delivery showing deft wristwork.
explanation.walkthrough: A leg break is a cricket delivery spun from leg side to off; here 'break' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand is a conjuror's manual dexterity, so the word means deftness.

clue.text: Cases prepared for Italian consumer groups

definitions.text: Cases prepared for Italian consumer groups

parts.words: Cases prepared for Italian consumer groups
parts.note: sounds like legal cases readied for Italian shoppers' associations, but the cases are little stuffed parcels of pasta to be eaten

explanation.surface: Lawsuits being readied for consumer organisations in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' suggests court cases, and 'consumer groups' lobby organisations; they are pasta cases and the people who eat them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small square pasta pockets filled with meat or cheese, a dish eaten in Italy.

clue.text: She gets the same bit of luck twice

indicators.note: says the same piece is written two times over

parts.note: a bit of the word luck, its opening two letters

explanation.surface: A woman who enjoys the same small slice of good fortune two times.
explanation.walkthrough: Lulu is a woman's name; it is also slang for something remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Lulu is a female name, so a woman can stand for it.

clue.text: Rene's upset by expression of contempt

indicators.note: the letters of Rene's are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Rene is hurt by a scornful look.
explanation.definitionFit: A scornful curl of the lip or mocking remark shows disdain.

clue.text: Left in charge

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned and put in command.
explanation.definitionFit: Food left over is remaining, and someone placed over others is their superior in authority.

clue.text: Mind you take this!

parts.note: the friendly parting phrase urges someone to look after themselves, so the missing word is what you should take

explanation.surface: A warning to be sure you pick something up.
explanation.definitionFit: To mind is to look after or be cautious, and taking caution is the parting advice.

clue.text: It turns up after an opponent

indicators.note: places the reversed piece after the word an

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means the word It is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: Something appears following a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' at the start looks like the clue's subject, but it is fodder; 'turns up' flips it in this down entry and 'after' places it behind AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone anti is against a thing, an informal noun for an objector.

clue.text: Spoil Sarah with a light wine

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
Sal is a pet form of the name Sarah
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ruining Sarah's evening with a glass of something light.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsala is a fortified wine from Sicily, used in cooking and desserts.

clue.text: Vessel almost departed with the wrong load

indicators.note: almost means the word for departed is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: gone means departed or left

indicators.note: the word load is put wrong, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship nearly left port carrying the wrong cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts GONE to GON; 'wrong' turns LOAD into DOLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondola is a Venetian boat, and a boat is a vessel.

clue.text: One who does may land in hot water-or cold

definitions.text: One who does may land in hot water-or cold

parts.words: One who does may land in hot water-or cold
parts.note: taking a risky course gets you into trouble, hot water; doing it literally on a frozen pond risks a plunge into cold water

explanation.surface: Warning that a reckless act can lead to trouble, or a freezing dunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means taking a dangerous risk, and a skater on a fragile frozen surface may fall through.
